goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — The migration dereferences the first category join result even though the default blank embed_category produces no row and aborts upgrades before fallback.
app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — A valid configured host with a port is stored with the port but lookup compares only URI.host, so the UI can save an allowed host that never authorizes embeds.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real bug. Looking at the diff, in `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, the `before_validation` callback strips the protocol and path from the host (`self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` and `self.host.sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`), but it does NOT strip the port. The validation regex at line 2 allows ports: `/\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i`. So a host like 'example.com:8080' can be saved. However, in `record_for_host` method (lines 10-17), it uses `uri.host` which returns only the hostname without the port. The comparison `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` would compare 'example.com' (from URI) against 'example.com:8080' (stored), which would never match. This is a real correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — Duplicate host rows can be created concurrently and the unordered first match makes the category selected for that host nondeterministic.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue in the new EmbeddableHost model. Looking at the diff, the `record_for_host` method at line 17 uses `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` without any ordering, and there's no unique constraint on the host column in the migration (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb shows only `t.string :host, null: false` without a unique index). This means duplicate hosts can be inserted, and the `.first` call without ordering would return a nondeterministic result. The category_id is then used in topic_embed.rb for posting to a category, so this could cause unpredictable behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:38 — Saving with no category overwrites the server-defaulted uncategorized relation with undefined, leaving the displayed model inconsistent until reload.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the save action in embeddable-host.js.es6 lines 29-38, after a successful save, it sets `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))`. The categoryId is initialized as null (line 9) and only set when editing an existing host (line 25). For a new host where no category is explicitly selected, categoryId remains null. The server defaults to uncategorized_category_id (line 24 of embeddable_hosts_controller.rb), but the client-side code will set the category to undefined (since findById(null) returns undefined), causing the displayed model to be inconsistent with what the server saved.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — A blank/default embed_category produces no join row, so indexing [0] crashes the upgrade before the uncategorized fallback.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the migration code at line 11: `category_id = execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. If embed_category is blank or doesn't match any category name, the query returns no rows, and accessing [0] on an empty result will raise an error (nil has no method []). The fallback to uncategorized_category_id on line 14 only runs if category_id == 0, but the code crashes before reaching that check. This is a real bug in the migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — The backfill copies URL-form host-list entries verbatim even though later lookup compares the URI hostname, so existing allow-list entries with a scheme/path stop authorizing embeds after the settings are deleted.

adjudication.rationale: The migration at line 25 copies host values directly from the old site_settings table with `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. The old embeddable_hosts setting could contain entries like 'http://example.com' or 'https://example.com/path'. However, the new EmbeddableHost model (app/models/embeddable_host.rb) has a before_validation callback that strips 'http://' and paths, and the host_allowed? method compares against URI(host).host. The migration doesn't apply this normalization, so migrated entries with schemes/paths will be stored verbatim but won't match during lookup since the comparison uses the parsed hostname only.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:31 — Deleting the legacy settings via execute inside change has no inverse, so rollback cannot restore the migrated configuration.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the migration uses `change` method but contains destructive operations (DELETE FROM site_settings) that cannot be automatically reversed. The `execute` statements at line 31 delete legacy settings, and Rails cannot generate an inverse for raw SQL. This means a rollback would fail to restore the original configuration. While this is a real concern about migration design, it's not a bug per se - the migration will work correctly going forward, but rollback capability is compromised. This is a legitimate architectural/design concern specific to this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3 — force: true drops an already-present embeddable_hosts table, losing its rows if this migration is replayed after a partial deployment or recovery.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that 'force: true' will drop an existing table if the migration is replayed. However, looking at the diff, the migration creates a new table 'embeddable_hosts' that didn't exist before (this is a new feature being added). Rails migrations are designed to run once and are tracked in schema_migrations table. The 'force: true' option is a standard practice in migrations to ensure the table is created fresh, and migrations are not meant to be 'replayed' in normal operation. The concern about 'partial deployment or recovery' is speculative and not a real defect in the context of how Rails migrations work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — Every embed authorization runs an unindexed `lower(host)` database scan instead of the previously cached setting lookup.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new EmbeddableHost.record_for_host method in app/models/embeddable_host.rb performs a database query with `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` on every embed authorization check. Looking at the diff, there's no index added in the migration (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb) for the host column, and the query uses `lower(host)` which would prevent using a standard index anyway. This replaces the previous in-memory SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? check. While this is a valid performance concern for a feature that could be called frequently, it's not a bug per se - the code will work correctly, just potentially slower. This is an architectural/performance concern that a reasonable reviewer might raise.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:11 — Updating a host deleted by another admin dereferences nil and returns a 500 instead of a handled not-found response.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb, the update method at line 11 does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then calls `save_host(host)`. If the host doesn't exist (deleted by another admin), `host` will be nil. The `save_host` method then tries to call `host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]` on nil, which would cause a NoMethodError (500 error) rather than a proper 404 response. The same issue exists in the destroy method. This is a real bug - there's no nil check before using the host object.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:16 — Deleting an already-deleted host dereferences nil and returns a 500 instead of a handled not-found response.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a bug in the destroy action at line 16. The code uses `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` which returns nil if the record doesn't exist, then calls `host.destroy` on it. If the host is nil (already deleted or never existed), this will raise a NoMethodError (calling destroy on nil), resulting in a 500 error instead of a proper 404 response. This is a real defect in the new code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:46 — A failed host deletion has no rejection handler, leaving the UI without an error message or recovery path.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 46 in app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6, the delete action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(...)` but there is no `.catch()` handler for the promise. In contrast, the save action on line 38 properly handles errors with `.catch(popupAjaxError)`. If the destroyRecord API call fails, the user will not see any error message and the UI will remain in an inconsistent state. This is a real defect in error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Interpolating legacy host values into SQL lets a quote in an existing setting execute arbitrary SQL during migration.

adjudication.rationale: The migration at line 25 uses string interpolation to insert host values directly into SQL: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. The host values come from existing site settings (embeddable_hosts) which could contain single quotes or other SQL injection characters. If a malicious or accidental value like `evil.com'; DROP TABLE users; --` was stored in the settings, it would execute arbitrary SQL during migration. This is a real SQL injection vulnerability in the migration code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:5 — The new host CRUD API has only an inheritance assertion, so create/update/delete and category assignment behavior are untested.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb only tests inheritance (line 7: 'expect(Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController).to eq(true)'). The diff shows the controller has create, update, and destroy actions with actual logic (save_host method, category_id handling, etc.) in app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb, but none of this behavior is tested. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly added nontrivial logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb:5 — The embedding endpoint has no response-serialization coverage, leaving the embeddable host/category relationship delivered to the admin UI unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new embedding controller spec (spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb) only tests that the controller is a subclass of AdminController, but doesn't test the actual response serialization. Looking at the diff, the EmbeddingController has show and update actions that render serialized data with EmbeddingSerializer, which includes embeddable_hosts with their category relationships. The spec at lines 1-9 only checks inheritance, not the actual JSON response structure. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly added functionality, though the embeddable_host_spec.rb does test the model behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:41 — No test verifies that importing an allowed URL creates its topic in that host's selected category.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims there's no test verifying that importing an allowed URL creates its topic in the host's selected category. However, looking at the diff in spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb, lines 36-38 show: 'expect(post.topic.category).to eq(embeddable_host.category)' - this is exactly the test that verifies the topic is created in the embeddable host's category. The finding is factually incorrect.
